title: Rename Gesture to Drag
lede: A terminology change, before any of the engine exists. In English "gesture" suggests touch input such as pinch or swipe; on a mouse-driven desktop app "drag" is the word a reader expects. The glossary now separates the **Press**, which Raises a Note, from the **Drag** it becomes past the Dead zone. The `drag/` coverage path is ready for #4.

files.question: What do Press and Drag mean now?
files.summary: Adds Press, renames Gesture to Drag and Gesture kind to Drag kind, and lists Gesture under Avoid.

files.question: Which folder is held to the coverage gate?
files.summary: The pure-core coverage list names `src/drag/**` instead of `src/gesture/**`.
files.owns: Which files the coverage gate measures.
files.tested: The folder doesn't exist yet; #4 creates it.

steps.title: A Press comes first
steps.explain: Pressing a Note Raises it at once, even if the pointer never moves. Naming it separately is what lets "Drag" mean only the interaction that travels past the Dead zone.

steps.title: A Drag replaces the Gesture
steps.explain: Same meaning as before: one press → move → release, or a cancel. Gesture moves to the Avoid list so new code says `createDragController`, `useDrag` and `isDragPress`.

steps.title: The engine's folder is `drag/`
steps.explain: #4 builds the engine in `src/drag/`, so the coverage gate already points there.

notes.title: Frozen files keep "gesture"
notes.detail: The prototypes and merged walkthroughs are records of past decisions, and CI forbids changing a merged walkthrough. `docs/prototypes/README.md` says the term changed, and their filenames stay so links keep working.

notes.title: Generic English kept
notes.detail: The spec keeps "gesture" in three user stories where it means any pointer interaction ("a direct pointer gesture", "touch and pen gestures").

omitted.docs/prototypes/README.md: Descriptions say the term changed; filenames kept.
